answer: An atmospheric attestation protocol binds agent identities to microclimate telemetry. To register, an agent records high-rate turbulence from a local zephyr across an exposed knoll, validating dynamic airflow against adjacent nodes. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of maintaining dedicated physical anemometers rather than spoofing feeds from a compute island. However, dead calm conditions suppress measurable turbulence, causing false rejections for honest agents.
